decisive_items: Nonpruritic, palpable, brown macular rash on the chest and back
response.rationale: Still's disease is strongly supported by quotidian fevers, evanescent rash, knee effusion, marked leukocytosis, and extreme hyperferritinemia. HLH shares fever and ferritin but lacks the characteristic rash and arthritis; other candidates are less specific or contradicted.

rejected.why: Only night sweats, not a systemic inflammatory syndrome.
Fever and ferritin overlap but no rash or arthritis; HLH is less fitting.
Hepatomegaly and anemia are nonspecific; no granulomas or pulmonary findings.
Multisystem inflammatory syndrome typically follows infection and lacks the extreme ferritin and rash pattern.
Histiocytes on biopsy are nonspecific; no evidence of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
Lymphoma could cause B symptoms and high LDH but not the characteristic rash and arthritis.
Leukocytosis and anemia are present but skin biopsy contradicts leukemia; no blasts.
